terms.definition: A command-line tool that automates installing, updating, and removing software packages, including resolving all dependencies automatically
terms.example: YUM on Amazon Linux — running 'sudo yum install git -y' downloads git and all its dependencies in one command

terms.definition: A central, trusted storage location of verified software packages from which Linux systems install and update software
terms.example: Amazon Linux's official repository at /etc/yum.repos.d/amazonlinux.repo — contains all packages available for installation

terms.definition: Yellowdog Updater, Modified — the default package manager for Amazon Linux, Red Hat, and CentOS systems
terms.example: sudo yum install nginx -y installs Nginx web server from the configured repository

terms.definition: Advanced Package Tool — the default package manager for Ubuntu and Debian-based Linux distributions, using .deb package format
terms.example: sudo apt install apache2 -y is the Ubuntu equivalent of sudo yum install httpd -y

terms.definition: Red Hat Package Manager — the package format used by Amazon Linux, Red Hat, and CentOS; files end in .rpm
terms.example: When you install Git with YUM, it downloads a .rpm file, unpacks it, and places executables in /usr/bin/

terms.definition: Another software library or program that a package requires in order to function correctly
terms.example: Git depends on several cryptography libraries — YUM automatically installs all 8 required packages when you install git

terms.definition: A compressed archive containing program files, dependencies, configuration files, and metadata — everything needed to install software
terms.example: The git package contains the git binary, required libraries, default config files, and version/license metadata

terms.definition: Applying small code updates to fix security vulnerabilities, resolve bugs, or improve performance without replacing the software completely
terms.example: Running sudo yum update git -y to apply a security fix to git without reinstalling or replacing the entire package

terms.definition: YUM command that refreshes the local repository metadata — tells the system which software versions are currently available — does NOT install anything
terms.example: sudo yum update -y should always be run before yum upgrade to ensure you're working with current repository information

terms.definition: YUM command that downloads and installs newer versions of all currently installed packages based on the latest repository metadata
terms.example: sudo yum upgrade -y updates Python from 3.9 to the latest 3.x version available in the repository

terms.definition: The first tier of a 3-tier web application — what users see and interact with in their browser, served by a web server like Apache or Nginx
terms.example: When you open flipkart.com and see the homepage, you are looking at the frontend tier running on a web server

terms.definition: The second tier of a 3-tier web application — processes business logic, handles user requests, and talks to the database
terms.example: When you click Login on a website, the backend (Node.js/Flask) validates your credentials and generates a response

terms.definition: An open-source web server software used to serve frontend web application files over HTTP/HTTPS
terms.example: sudo yum install httpd -y installs Apache on Amazon Linux — the package name is httpd, not apache

terms.definition: A high-performance web server and reverse proxy known for handling large numbers of concurrent connections with low memory usage
terms.example: Nginx is commonly used for high-traffic sites and as a reverse proxy in front of Node.js or Flask backend servers

terms.definition: An open-source relational database management system used as the Tier 3 data store in 3-tier web applications
terms.example: When you log into a website, the backend queries MySQL to check if your username and password match stored records

terms.definition: A web application design pattern with three layers: Frontend (web server), Backend (application server), and Database — each with a distinct responsibility
terms.example: Netflix uses 3-tier architecture — Nginx serves the UI, Java/Python backends handle recommendations, and databases store user data

terms.definition: Core Linux programs that run and manage the operating system itself — without these, Linux would not function
terms.example: The Linux kernel, bash shell, and systemd are all system software that come pre-installed with the OS

terms.definition: Programs that provide specific functionality to end users or services — installed by administrators for business purposes
terms.example: Apache, MySQL, Git, and Python are application software — you install them based on what your server needs to do

terms.definition: Supporting helper tools used to manage and maintain the Linux system — not the main application but essential for administration
terms.example: vim (text editor), chmod (permissions), ls (list files), and tar (compression) are all utility software

terms.definition: A cryptographic signature that verifies a software package was published by the official repository maintainer and has not been tampered with
terms.example: When YUM downloads a package, it automatically verifies the GPG signature before installing — protecting against malicious packages

terms.definition: The service manager for modern Linux systems that starts, stops, and monitors background services and processes
terms.example: sudo systemctl start httpd uses systemd to start the Apache web server service

terms.definition: An AWS service that automates OS patching across EC2 instances without requiring manual SSH access to each server
terms.example: Use Patch Manager to apply security patches to 100 EC2 instances simultaneously on a defined schedule
